sources.title: CUCM 15 Reporting and Billing Administration Guide
sources.claim: Overview of CUCM CDR/CMR reporting and billing. Other current CUCM 15 sections establish the split file types, SFTP delivery, billing setup, and formats; this skill encodes no maximum billing-server count because current Cisco pages conflict.

sources.title: CUCM 15 Reporting and Billing Administration - billing server setup
sources.claim: Current billing-server setup evidence. Cisco CUCM 15 pages conflict on the supported maximum, so the router records no maximum.

sources.title: CUCM 15 Reporting and Billing Administration - export and CDR/CMR distinction
sources.claim: CDR and CMR are distinct SFTP-delivered file types and must be collected and evidenced independently.

sources.title: CUCM 15 Export CDRs and CMRs - exported CDR type-row mapping
sources.claim: The current exported CDR type row maps callingPartyNumber and finalCalledPartyNumber to VARCHAR(50).

sources.title: CUCM 15 Call Management Records - corresponding sample CMR type-row mapping
sources.claim: Corresponding Sample CMRs maps globalCallID_callId to INTEGER and directoryNum to VARCHAR(50). This is the only exported CMR pair eligible for locally_evidence_qualified in this router.

sources.title: CUCM 15 Reporting and Billing Administration - record and file format
sources.claim: Current CDR/CMR record and file format evidence: line 1 contains unique field names, line 2 contains equally wide nonempty field types, and lines 3 onward contain equally wide data records. CDR and CMR files remain distinct.

sources.title: CUCM 15 CDR field descriptions
sources.claim: The cdrRecordType field is always 1 for CDR records. Current CDR field naming uses globalCallID_callManagerId and globalCallID_callId. Cisco declares the manager ID, call ID, and origLegCallIdentifier as Positive Integer; other fields declared Integer receive no invented bounds.

sources.title: CUCM 15 CMR field descriptions
sources.claim: The cdrRecordType field is always 2 for CMR records. globalCallId_callId with directoryNumber is field-description compatibility only; globalCallID_callManagerId is stable. Cisco declares the manager ID, documented call-ID field, nodeId, and callIdentifier as Positive Integer; jitter is unsigned; numberPacketsLost may be negative; date/time and latency remain ordinary Integer fields without invented bounds.

sources.title: CUCM CLI reference for the CDR repository
sources.claim: cm/cdr_repository and cm/cdr_repository/processed/<date> are diagnostic CLI paths, not the external billing export contract.

sources.title: CUCM 15 Administration Guide - remote audit log transfer protocol
sources.claim: This authority applies specifically to CUCM remote audit logging. Its normal-mode default protocol is UDP and utils remotesyslog set protocol can select UDP, TCP, or TLS. TLS supports unidirectional or bidirectional x.509 authentication and certificate trust requirements. The page does not establish a receiver-port default or transport support for every generic CUCM service-syslog path, so this router requires an explicit operator-selected port and makes no broader device-transport claim.

sources.title: AXL Developer Guide
sources.claim: AXL is a throttled provisioning/configuration SOAP/XML API using HTTPS POST to the CUCM publisher, normally /axl/ on port 8443; it is not a realtime CDR collection API.

sources.title: Cisco Expressway Administrator Guide X15.5 - serviceability, logging, monitoring, and metrics
sources.claim: Expressway remote syslog wire modes are legacy BSD or IETF over UDP port 514, or IETF over TLS port 6514 with trust requirements. CDR is off by default and can emit INFO records to syslog; media statistics use local2. SC4S listener capabilities are a separate contract.

sources.title: Cisco Meeting Server 3.13 product and support page
Cisco Meeting Server MMP Command Reference 3.13
sources.claim: CMS 3.13 remote syslog uses TCP, not UDP. Prefixing the server with tls: enables the optional TLS form; this device contract is separate from SC4S listener and certificate readiness.

sources.title: Cisco Meeting Server CDR Guide 3.11 and later
sources.claim: Current CDR authority: CMS sends XML CDR records to external HTTP(S) receivers and does not retain them as a long-term internal store.

sources.title: Cisco Meeting Server CDR Guide 3.7 and later, version 3.10 copy
Cisco Meeting Management 3.13 Installation and Configuration Guide
sources.claim: CMM 3.13 configures system and audit log servers independently, with up to five of each. It supports UDP, TCP, and TLS; TLS uses TLS 1.2, and receivers must accept messages up to 8192 bytes. This router models explicit TCP or TLS sender profiles, defaults the privacy-safe example to TLS, and keeps SC4S TLS listener/certificate readiness unresolved without claiming live configuration.

sources.title: SC4S sources and custom product-port mapping
sources.claim: SC4S custom mappings use SC4S_LISTEN_{VENDOR}_{PRODUCT}_{PROTOCOL}_PORT and require a port dedicated exclusively to that device/product mapping. A bare child render without the exact reviewed port binding does not establish listener readiness.

sources.title: SC4S 3.29 custom port troubleshooting
sources.claim: Versioned SC4S troubleshooting evidence reiterates the vendor/product/protocol listener-port pattern and exclusive-port requirement; it does not prove that this router's bare CUCM child argv opens an operator-selected port.

sources.title: Splunk Cloud Platform 10.5.2605 fields command
sources.claim: Official fields-command authority: inclusion form retains the internal _raw and _time fields unless they are explicitly removed, while timechart requires _time. The privacy search therefore projects _time and collaboration_route, explicitly removes _raw as the final pre-aggregation step, and then runs timechart.
